decisions.reason: The buzzer-specific prototype and production sourcing allowance does not change the selected LED part or its electrical interface.
The source concerns selection of a passive buzzer part and does not alter the sensor-board connector matrix.
The SPS30 I2C operating mode and SEL pin connection are independent of the buzzer sourcing decision.
The buzzer part allowance does not change the panel reset connector, mounting, or electrical action.
The panel button and switch inputs are semantically unaffected by the buzzer prototype and production part policy.
The source does not change provision or behavior of the PIR sensor connector.
References to LCSC and parts are incidental overlap; the source identifies only a buzzer and does not revise the LED array board part.
The capacitive touch connectors, sensors, and GPIO assignments remain unchanged.

The message establishes a buzzer-specific prototype-versus-production sourcing allowance already owned by the buzzer Requirement; it does not revise the existing general and USB-connector sourceability rules.
The buzzer sourcing choice does not affect interboard power connectors, topology, or pinout.
The source does not alter any interboard signal connector selection or pin assignment.
The buzzer part sourcing allowance has no effect on I2C cable, pull-up, speed, or series-resistor requirements.
